title: PCS Moves = Family Routine Reset
intro: A permanent change of station (PCS) move may feel stressful, but it also creates a unique opportunity to reset family routines and build healthier habits.

sections.markdown:
When Wi-Fi isn't set up, boxes still need unpacking, and daily schedules are disrupted, families can be more open to trying something new.

This natural pause allows you to reset expectations, rebuild structure, and create routines that support a smoother daily rhythm.

sections.heading: Rebuild Daily Routines
sections.markdown:
Because PCS moves naturally disrupt old habits, they provide an ideal opportunity to establish new routines.

Focus on creating calmer mornings, consistent evening wind-downs, shared meals, and bedtime routines that support quality sleep and overall well-being.

sections.heading: Reset Digital Boundaries
sections.markdown:
With internet access temporarily limited, screen time may already be reduced. Take advantage of this moment to introduce screen-free zones, shared charging stations, and consistent device-free times, especially during meals or conversations.

A PCS transition offers a fresh start to build stronger family connections through more intentional, face-to-face interaction.

sections.heading: Build a Chore System That Works
sections.markdown:
A new home brings new responsibilities. This is a great time to create a simple chore system that fits your space and schedule.

Assign age-appropriate tasks, rotate responsibilities, and consider a weekly "family reset" hour to keep the household running smoothly. Clear expectations help everyone understand their role and contribute to the team.

sections.heading: Strengthen Communication Habits
sections.markdown:
Transitions can bring stress, excitement, and a range of emotions.

Establishing regular check-ins, quick "what do you need today?" conversations and using shared calendars can help families stay connected and aligned during times of change.

sections.heading: Need Additional Support?
sections.markdown: For more resources on strengthening family routines and communication, connect with your installation's [Family Advocacy Program (FAP)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/fap) or [Community Counseling Program (CCP)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/ccp).
